---
title: "Averaging error shares across reports"
subtitle: "2.19 · after the postrank theory book, chapters 8 and 16"
description: "Pooled errors, conditional mean error shares and zero-imputed means when disclosure varies."
---

When disclosure varies across outcomes, several averages of error shares are possible. The ratio of expected wrong
and stated counts weights outcomes in proportion to disclosure. The mean of the defined report fractions instead
conditions on positive disclosure and weights those outcomes by their probabilities. Assigning zero to outcomes with
no disclosure yields a third quantity. The examples calculate all three from common counts and probabilities,
including a randomisation over complete reports and a repeated-dataset simulation. Their differences follow from
their denominators and the treatment of outcomes with no stated direction.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Three outcomes.** Pooled pairs give 2/5, the mean among disclosing outcomes is 1/2, and zero-imputation gives
  1/3. The chance of disclosure is 2/3 and mean disclosure is 5/9. Changes to wrong and stated counts affect these summaries differently because their denominators differ. The silent outcome has an undefined fraction.
- **More weight on errors.** Giving the error-heavy outcome more probability changes the pooled ratio to 4/7,
  the disclosing mean to 2/3 and the zero-imputed mean to 1/2. Relative weights are normalised; they describe the
  distribution over outcomes, rather than extra units inside an outcome.
- **A complete-report lottery.** The four-unit example mixes entire reports. Pooled expected counts give 1/8,
  while the mean report fraction is 49/400. The lottery probability weights each complete report and its disclosure.
  Expected weighted errors are averaged within a report before the reporting lottery is applied.
- **All silent.** Both ratio-based summaries read “NA: no disclosure”; the zero-imputed mean is 0. That zero is a
  convention, not evidence that a disclosed direction was accurate. The probability of any disclosure is reported separately.
- **Twenty datasets.** A simulated league gives pooled error .0892 and a disclosing mean .0891. The running curves and individual counts describe the averages over the selected number of datasets. The true values stay fixed while each
  dataset produces fresh estimates and its own graded report.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
A ratio estimated from a small sample need not be unbiased for a ratio of expectations. The hand-set outcomes
provide an exact single-observation example; one trajectory of simulated datasets shows variability, rather than
measuring that bias. Simple rational values use fractions in the finite examples; simulated shares use the site's decimal format.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In R"}
```r
A <- c(2, 0, 0); N <- c(2, 3, 0)
c(pooled=sum(A)/sum(N), disclosing=mean((A/N)[N>0]), zero_imputed=mean(ifelse(N>0,A/N,0)))
```
:::

Standalone: [averaging-errors](../../embed/averaging-errors.html), for example `?mode=replays&replays=5&cap=1`.
